name: CopyClip v0.2.3
body:
## Highlights

- **Custom open shortcut** — the Open‑shortcut dropdown now has a **Custom…** entry: press any combination to bind your own, since the built‑in presets often clash with existing system shortcuts.
- **Panel icon** — an optional tray/panel icon with **Show Clipboard · Settings · Quit**, on desktops that support status icons (GNOME with the AppIndicator extension, KDE, XFCE, …). Toggle it under Settings → Behaviour.

Plus minor memory‑usage optimizations — a lighter idle footprint and leaner per‑image handling.

name: v0.2.2 — CopyClip is back 👋
body:
## CopyClip is back 👋

Back in February I [stepped away](https://github.com/Walkercito/CopyClip/issues/5#issuecomment-3881059497) — I said there was still a lot for me to learn, and that I didn't want to ship something buggy or hard to set up. So I went and learned, and I rebuilt CopyClip from scratch.

It's a **native C++ app with a GTK4 / libadwaita UI** now, and the thing that caused the most pain is finally solved:

> **One hotkey, working on both X11 and Wayland, set up for you — nothing to wire by hand.**

### What's new since I left
- Rewritten in C++23 — faster, lighter, event-driven (no polling)
- The same global shortcut on X11 **and** Wayland, configured automatically
- A one-line installer that ships a native `.deb` / `.rpm` / AppImage for your distro (or builds from source) and sets up autostart
- Text, rich-text, and image history, with pinning and fuzzy search
- Click a clip to paste it straight into the app you came from — terminals included
- Dark, light, or system theme

### Install
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Walkercito/CopyClip/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

🌐 **Website:** https://copyclip-eta.vercel.app/

Back when I stepped away (#5, #6) I pointed everyone to another great clipboard manager and thanked you for the stars and the issues — that genuinely meant a lot. CopyClip's back now, the issues are open again, and I'd love for you to give it another try.

It's still young software (v0.2.2), so expect rough edges on setups I haven't tested. Thanks for the patience. ❤️

name: v0.1.4
body: CopyClip v0.1.4 — Official Release --- A stable and refined release following the v0.1.2 pre-testing build. This version completes the internal restructuring of the project and delivers a smoother, more reliable experience across multiple desktop environments. ### What’s New - Complete rewrite and re-organization of the project structure - Fully modular architecture for easier maintenance and future development - Added support for both Wayland (wtype, ydotool) and X11 (xdotool) - Polished and refined UI for overall better usability - Added a Welcome Window for first-time users - Clipboard UI now auto-refreshes on every copy action - Duplicate entries now move to the top instead of being recreated - New option to prevent the window from closing after copying (Settings) - New option to auto-paste into the focused window (Settings) - Expanded flexibility for the settings.json configuration --- ### Bug Fixes - Fixed multiple instances of the app launching when pressing the hotkey - Fixed hotkey incorrectly typing into the active application

name: v0.1.2 pre-testing Release
body:
### v0.1.2 Implementations
---

- **Complete rewrite and re-organization of the project structure**
- **Full modularization** for easier future development
- Added support for **Wayland** (wtype, ydotool) and **X11** (xdotool)
- Refined and polished the UI
- Added a **welcome window** for first-time users
- UI auto-refresh on copy action
- Duplicates now move to the top instead of creating a new entry
- Added option to prevent the window from closing on copy (Settings)
- Added option to auto-paste to the focused window (Settings)
- Added more flexibility to the `settings.json` file

### Bug Fixes
---

- Fixed multiple instances of the app running when pressing the hotkey
- Fixed hotkey incorrectly typing into the focused application

**Special thanks to**  
- @peterjosvai — bug reports and feature suggestions  #4 
- @fonziemedia — auto-paste feature request #2 #3

name: CopyClip v0.1 Stable Release
body:
**CopyClip**: Open-Source Clipboard Manager for Linux

CopyClip is an open-source clipboard manager for Linux, inspired by the advanced clipboard features of Windows 10. Effortlessly manage your clipboard history with intuitive controls and quick access to your most recent items.

## What's New in v0.1 Stable

- **Framework Migration**: Transitioned from CustomTkinter to PyQt6 to resolve compatibility issues
- **Modernized UI**: Completely redesigned interface using CSS styling in PyQt6
- **Intuitive Interaction Model**:
  - Click directly on any item to copy it
  - Ctrl+Click to pin important items
  - No more dedicated buttons needed for common actions
- **New Keyboard Shortcuts**: Added Ctrl+ESC to quickly exit the application
- **Various Bug Fixes**: Multiple improvements to enhance stability and performance

Thanks to @fonziemedia for suggesting the improved click-based copy/pin functionality in issue #1!

name: v0.0.1-alpha
body:
# CopyClip: Open-Source Clipboard Manager for Linux

**CopyClip** is an open-source clipboard manager for Linux, inspired by the advanced clipboard features of Windows 10. Effortlessly manage your clipboard history with intuitive controls and quick access to your most recent items.

---

## ✨ Features

- 🗂️ **Clipboard History**: Track all copied items in reverse chronological order.  
- 📌 **Pin Important Items**: Save crucial snippets by pinning them to the top of your clipboard history.  
- 🎛️ **Customizable Shortcuts**: Configure shortcuts for quick access and management.  
- 🔄 **Auto-clear on Reboot**: Automatically clear your clipboard history upon reboot (with the option to keep pinned items).  
- 🖼️ **Simple UI**: Access your clipboard history through a clean, user-friendly interface.
